Authorization: Bearer jxr_…

A prebuilt onyx-engine, checked against its release checksums, lands in the data directory.

One setting. Its adapter subclasses the llama.cpp one: same spawn, streaming and restart code.

Bound to 127.0.0.1, polled at /health, its OpenAI endpoints proxied through.

Apps and paired devices reach it through JX Runtime's keys, TLS and rate limits.

From a stock JX Runtime to Onyx Engine in four steps.

Compare engines on the same models.

terminal

$ jx-runtime dual-engine plan # prints, changes nothing

$ jx-runtime dual-engine setup --yes

$ jx-runtime serve # :8712 llama.cpp

$ jx-runtime serve --data-dir ~/.jx-runtime-onyx # :8713 Onyx Engine

SIDE BY SIDE

The secondary borrows the primary's model folders. Keys, pairing and the audit log are per instance and never copied.

jx-runtime dual-engine runs two instances on the same model files.

Same contract. Same code path.

NO SECOND COPY

/health

Polled until ready. For onyx-engine, ready means the model is loaded.

/props

Context, template hash and build info, read once after start.

/v1/*

Chat, completions and embeddings proxied straight through, streaming included.

restart

Crash detection and failure classification are the llama.cpp adapter's own code.

The onyxengine adapter subclasses the llama.cpp adapter.

Run it on your machine. Share it on your terms.
